free_text: The 72-year-old male presents with an elevated PSA of 8.7 ng/mL and a prior biopsy showing ISUP grade group 1 cancer. MRI revealed a PI-RADS 3 lesion, and the clinical stage is cT1c. Given the low-grade pathology and imaging findings, active surveillance is recommended to weigh treatment benefit against patient preferences. The trade-off involves monitoring for progression versus the risks and benefits of intervention for a low-grade disease.
